item.title: Food and drink: feeding a room that's working
item.description:
Feeding a room that's working is a different job to feeding a party.
People are watching the clock. Somebody has to stand up at two. Lunch has forty minutes and it has to be finished when it says it's finished, because the afternoon session doesn't move for anybody.
That's a normal booking here. The function room takes up to 100 standing, and the bar takes 30 for the drinks at the end, which is where most of the actual conversations happen anyway. We're a short walk from the seafront and close to the BIC. And yours is the only event in the building that day, so the timings are yours.
If your name is the one on the booking, you want the answers before you can shortlist anybody.
Ring 01202 144484 and tell us the date … we'll come back with what you need.

item.title: The weekend feeling
item.description:
Last Friday of the month, which makes this about the right time to say it … the good December dates go early.
Not a scare tactic. It's just that everybody wants the same three Saturdays, and the people who get them are the ones thinking about it in September while the rest of us are still pretending it's summer.
If you're the one who ends up organising the work do, or there's a birthday that got pushed back over the summer, it's a calmer conversation now than in six weeks' time.
Save this and come back to it when the clocks change.

item.title: Something real: the room for a cause
item.description:
Every committee ends up needing a room, and usually at short notice.
Charity nights. Fundraising dinners. Round Table evenings. The annual thing that has to happen whether anybody volunteers for it or not. They all want the same handful of things … a room that can be dressed, a bar, food timed around the raffle instead of across it, and somewhere the speeches can actually be heard.
That's what this room does. A night that raises money is a good night for it to have in the diary.
Share this with whoever's got the job on your committee.

item.title: The spaces: the garden opens
item.description:
The garden is finished.
It's been a building site all summer, which is why you've never seen a photograph of it from us. That changes now. From October it's the third space here alongside the function room and the bar.
It takes up to 20 out there, with the function room and the bar a few steps inside, so weather never ends a day here. A drinks reception that starts outside. A christening lunch where the children can be children. The bit between the ceremony and the sit-down when everybody wants air and nobody wants a speech.
Photographs shortly. We're not showing it to you until it's worth showing you.
Full details on our outdoor events page → ashburylounge.com/outdoor-bbq-events-bournemouth
What would you do out there first?

item.title: An occasion: wakes
item.description:
The wake is usually the part nobody has planned for.
It falls to one person, in the week they have the least room for it, and it has to be arranged in a few days.
We keep it simple. One room, set quietly before you arrive. Tea, sandwiches, something warm if you want it. Numbers often move late, and that is not a problem here.
If anyone coming has trouble with steps, say so when you ring and we will plan around it.
Full details on our wakes page → ashburylounge.com/wakes-celebration-of-life-bournemouth
Ring 01202 144484 and we will take it from there.

item.title: A straight answer: access
item.description:
Straight answer Wednesday. This week: "is it accessible?"
Here's the whole of it, in plain terms.
The bar is step-free. The function room is reached by three small steps. There is an accessible WC.
No lift to explain, no long corridor, nothing else to find out on the morning. And if somebody coming to your event can't manage three steps, tell us when you book and we'll work the day around it … which usually means using the bar for the parts they need to be at, and bringing people to them.
It's the question guests are too polite to ask and organisers worry about for weeks.
That's the last straight answer of the month. More of these in October.

item.title: The weekend feeling
item.description:
There's a particular half hour before every party where everything is ready and nothing has started.
The lights are doing their thing across an empty floor. The tables are set. Somebody is always still in the car park on the phone.
Then the door goes and it's gone.
Nobody who hires a room ever sees that half hour. We get it every time, and it's the best part of the job.
What's the bit you'd want to walk into?

item.title: The spaces: the dance floor
item.description:
The floor is already down, and it stays down.
Fixed, centre of the room, seating around it. Nothing gets built for your date and nothing gets lifted after it.
Which matters for one plain reason … what you stand on at the viewing is what your guests stand on at eleven o'clock. There's no version of this room you haven't already seen.
It works at both ends, too. The function room takes up to 100 standing, and the floor sits in the middle of it for a party of forty just the same.
Full details on our celebrations page → ashburylounge.com/celebrations-bournemouth
Viewings are by appointment. Ring 01202 144484 and come and stand on it.

item.title: An occasion: weddings, evening only
item.description:
Not every wedding needs a venue for the whole day.
Plenty of couples marry somewhere else … a church, the register office, somewhere further along the coast … and then need somewhere for the evening that isn't a marquee and a generator.
That's a straightforward booking here. The room is yours, the floor is down, we run the bar and the kitchen does the food. You walk in to a room that's already set.
Up to 100 standing for the reception, with the bar taking another 30 on its own if people want somewhere quieter for a bit … which, by about ten o'clock, some of them will. Usually the ones who've been on their feet since the ceremony.
Full details on our weddings page → ashburylounge.com/weddings-bournemouth
Viewings are by appointment. Ring 01202 144484.

item.title: A straight answer: can we look round first?
item.description:
Straight answer Wednesday. This week: "can we come and look round before we commit to anything?"
Yes, and you should. Nobody should book a room from photographs.
Viewings here are by appointment, so there are no opening hours to turn up inside. You ring, we find a time that suits you, and the room is free and lit when you get here, not mid-turnaround with a hoover in it.
Bring whoever's going to have an opinion. It's a much shorter conversation in the room than it is on the phone.
Ring 01202 144484 and we'll sort you a time.

item.title: Food and drink: the christening table
item.description:
The church gives you the time. Everything after it is yours to work out, and it usually lands on one person.
A christening lunch is a particular shape. Three generations in one room, a couple of car seats under the table, somebody's nan who needs to sit down and stay sat down, and a two-hour window where everyone eats at once and then goes home for a sleep.
So the food is built for that. Catering here is in-house as standard, canapés through to a sit-down, and a buffet built to get eaten in the middle of the range. There's genuine flexibility as well … Asian and cultural weddings, special menus, dietary requirements. Ask us early, that's a conversation we want to have.
The room is set before you arrive, so the family walks in from the church to somewhere ready.
Full details on our christenings page → ashburylounge.com/christenings-bournemouth
Share this with whoever's got the church date in their calendar.

item.title: The weekend feeling
item.description:
The letters go on and the room changes.
Same floor, same chandelier, same windows that were full of daylight an hour ago. Warm light up the walls, candles down, and it stops being a room and starts being an evening.
Most people commit to this bit having only ever seen the daylight version, which is honest and bright and tells you almost nothing about ten o'clock.
Which version would you want to see first?

item.title: Something real: the turnaround
item.description:
Chairs go on last.
Linens on, candelabra out, flowers in, floor swept. Chairs go on last, because they're the part that changes depending on what the room is doing that day.
Two hours of somebody else's work that nobody ever sees. Tables going down, the kitchen already going, the bar being set. By the time the first guest walks in, none of it is visible, and that is the point.
What's the bit of an event you'd never want to have to do yourself?

item.title: The spaces: the bar
item.description:
You wouldn't guess this was behind the door.
Green velvet, brass, a plant wall and a saxophone on it.
It takes 30 on its own, which makes it a room in its own right … a birthday for a dozen, drinks before something else, or the quieter end of a bigger night when a few people want to hear each other speak.
You don't have to take the function room to be here, and plenty of good evenings never leave this side of the building.
Ring 01202 144484 and tell us the number you've got in mind.

item.title: An occasion: milestone birthdays
item.description:
Balloons, candles, and a table that took somebody an hour.
Milestone birthdays are the bookings where the detail matters most and the organiser has the least time … usually because the organiser is also the one who always ends up doing it. The 70th for a dad who's told everyone he doesn't want a fuss. The 40th that got pushed back twice and is now happening whether it's convenient or not.
Here, the detail is the part we take off you. The floor's down, the room is set before anyone arrives, and the food comes out of our own kitchen. On the day, the person who built the party gets to be at it.
Ring 01202 144484 and tell us the date you're working towards.

item.title: A straight answer: one event at a time
item.description:
Straight answer Wednesday. This week: "how many events do you run at once?"
One.
That's the layout rather than a policy. There is one function room, one bar and one garden here, and that's the whole building … so on your date, the whole of it is yours.
Worth asking wherever you're looking, because the answer isn't the same everywhere and it changes what a day feels like from the inside.
What else would you want a straight answer on? Ask below and we'll take it in October.
